title: Partial Derivatives Are Slopes of Slices
topic: Define the partial derivatives of f(x,y) by slicing the surface z=f(x,y) with planes of constant y or constant x. The intersection is a one-variable curve whose slope at the point is the partial derivative.

beats.narration: Two inputs, one output — so which slope are we even talking about?

elements.content: Manimo bobs in centre-screen
Which slope?

beats.narration: Here is a surface z equals f of x and y. To talk about slope, freeze one input. Hold y at one fixed value — the surface intersected with that plane is a single curve in x and z.

elements.content: Oblique 3D axes — x right, y back-right, z up
Surface mesh — wireframe of constant-x and constant-y isolines on z=f(x,y)
Translucent vertical slice plane at y = y0
Highlighted intersection curve on the surface (1D parabola in x)
freeze y, vary x
z = f(x, y0)

beats.narration: Sweep the slice plane through different y values. Each y gives its own curve. The slope of that curve at the chosen x is the partial derivative of f with respect to x.

elements.content: Slice plane sweeping y from -1.2 to +1.2
Family of cross-section curves z(x) for each y; active one bright, others faded
Tangent line at x = x0 on the active curve
∂f/∂x = slope at x0
∂f/∂x = lim h→0 [f(x0+h, y0) − f(x0, y0)] / h

beats.narration: Now swap roles. Freeze x at x zero and slice the surface the other way. The intersection curve runs along y, and its slope is the partial derivative of f with respect to y.

elements.content: Slice plane now perpendicular — x = x0, sweeping x from -1.2 to +1.2
Cross-section curve z(y) at the active x
Tangent line at y = y0 on the curve
∂f/∂y = slope along y at y0
∂f/∂y = lim h→0 [f(x0, y0+h) − f(x0, y0)] / h

beats.narration: Two slopes through the same point — one along each axis. Together they make the gradient. Slicing was the whole trick.

elements.content: Two slopes, one point.
Each partial is a one-variable derivative — slope of a slice.
